standard_prerequisites.name: Descent of finite presentation from a ring to a quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts finite presentation over $R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ into finite presentation as an $S$-module, which is the conclusion of Part (2).

core_obligations: Obtain Part (1) as the special case of the finite type flat algebra statement over an integral base (proof lines 4221-4222).

For Part (2), choose a surjection $R[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to S$ and apply the module statement to conclude that $M$ is finitely presented over the polynomial ring, using flatness of $M$ over $R$ and finiteness over $S$ (proof lines 4223-4225).
Descend finite presentation along the quotient to the algebra $S$ itself (proof lines 4226-4227).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) as a special case (proof lines 4221-4222).
Lifting to a polynomial algebra and finite presentation there (proof lines 4223-4225).
difficulty_reason: The proposition records that over a domain, flatness upgrades finite type to finite presentation for the algebra and finiteness to finite presentation for a flat module over a finite type algebra (statement lines 4209-4218). The first part is quoted as a special case of a lemma, while the second chooses a polynomial presentation of the algebra, applies the module version of the same result over the polynomial ring, and descends along the quotient. The reduction to the polynomial ring and the descent are the substance, so the claim is H2.
